name: Isopropyl cloprostenate

lead: Isopropyl cloprostenate is a prostaglandin analogue found in some cosmetic eyelash growth serums. Prostaglandin analogues are a drug class whose side effects include increased eyelash growth, which is why they were adopted for lash enhancement.

The appearance payoff is longer, thicker and fuller-looking lashes. Researchers have reported that serums containing prostaglandin analogues are sold as cosmetics while not being regulated as such, and case reports describe periocular discoloration and hollowing in some users.

paras: The serum is applied along the lash line with a brush, typically as a regular routine, and lash changes are described as appearing over weeks of consistent use. People who use these serums often compare them with the prescription bimatoprost product and with false lashes.

Case reports describe darkened periorbital skin and periorbital fat or volume loss with prostaglandin lash serums, and a 2017 case of discoloration that faded after stopping the serum. Prostaglandin analogue drugs are also associated with iris pigmentation changes. A 2026 French analysis flagged the lack of regulation for such cosmetics.

angle.text: The ingredient works by the same class effect that makes glaucoma prostaglandin drops grow lashes as a side effect. Users apply it for fuller, longer lashes without extensions.

lead: Isopropyl cloprostenate is a synthetic prostaglandin analogue used as an active ingredient in cosmetic eyelash serums. Prostaglandin analogues were developed as glaucoma treatments, and Wikipedia lists increased eyelash growth, iris pigmentation and darkening of the skin around the eye among their side effects [1]. The lash-lengthening effect led to their remarketing as lash serums [2].

A 2026 qualitative study in France examined 79 cosmetic lash products and found that about 30 percent contained a prostaglandin analogue, with six different analogues identified; the most common were ethyl tafluprostamide (also called DDDE) and isopropyl cloprostenate [3]. The authors noted that these serums pose problems because they are not regulated for use in cosmetic products [3].

Published reports describe adverse effects. A 2017 case report described a 32-year-old woman with periocular discoloration after using an isopropyl cloprostenate serum, which gradually resolved after she stopped [4]. A 2022 aesthetic surgery journal study reported a case of thinner, darker skin and periorbital hollowing after 10 months of use and compared manufacturer before-and-after photos, asking whether prostaglandin lash serums cause eyelid fat and volume loss [2].
infobox: Not regulated for use in cosmetic products per a 2026 French study [3]

paras: The cosmetic use is lash enhancement. Prostaglandin analogues cause lengthening and thickening of lashes as a side effect, and manufacturers marketed serums with them for that effect [2]. In the French study, hydroalcoholic solutions made up most of the 79 serums examined, and some other products relied on ingredients like castor oil, amino acids, panthenol and peptides instead [3].

A case report described periocular discoloration after an isopropyl cloprostenate serum, with confocal microscopy showing small white spots in the perifollicular dermis and dilated vessels, a pattern reported earlier with prostaglandin analogues; it gradually faded after discontinuation [4]. Periorbital volume loss is a well-established side effect of topical prostaglandin analogues used for glaucoma, and a 2022 study explored whether lash-serum users show the same changes [2]. Wikipedia lists iris pigmentation and darkening of skin around the eye among the class effects [1].

The 2026 study concluded that prostaglandin analogue lash serums are available and promoted as lash growth treatments but are not regulated for use in cosmetic products [3]. Manufacturers describe their products as cosmetic; researchers note that the same ingredient class is used in drugs.

The published literature consists of case reports and informal analyses. The 2022 study combined a case report with a blinded grading of manufacturer photographs for signs of periorbital fat loss [2]. A 2017 case report used confocal microscopy to examine discoloration after use [4]. A 2026 product survey identified the analogues in marketed serums [3].
